name: Semaglutide

b.x: 14.9% of body weight gone in 68 weeks. That number, from the STEP 1 trial (n=1,961) [1], turned semaglutide into the most prescribed weight loss drug in modern medicine. Semaglutide (CAS 910463-68-2) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist sold as Ozempic, Wegovy, Wegovy HD, and Rybelsus. The drug mimics incretin hormone GLP-1. It binds receptors in the pancreas, the gut, and satiety centers in the hypothalamus. Pancreatic binding increases insulin secretion. Gut binding slows gastric emptying. Brain binding turns down hunger signals. An albumin-binding fatty acid side chain extends the half-life to roughly 7 days, allowing once-weekly dosing. Real-world use spans three FDA indications. Obesity patients follow the Wegovy titration from 0.25 mg up to 2.4 mg weekly (or 7.2 mg with the high-dose label approved March 2026). Type 2 diabetics typically land between 0.5 and 2.0 mg weekly on the Ozempic label. Cardiovascular patients stay at 2.4 mg long-term after SELECT [2] confirmed a 20% reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events across 17,604 participants. Community experience tracks the clinical data closely. Over 350,000 combined members across r/Ozempic and r/semaglutide consistently report appetite suppression, steady 1 to 2 lbs per week weight loss, and reduced food noise within the first month. The honest caveat: two-thirds of the weight returns within a year of stopping (STEP 1 extension data). Lean mass loss of 25 to 40% without resistance training is well-documented. This is a long-term commitment, not a quick fix. In SURMOUNT-5 (n=751) [10], semaglutide produced 13.7% weight loss versus 20.2% for tirzepatide at 72 weeks, with everyone on the highest dose they tolerated. Semaglutide holds the stronger cardiovascular outcomes dataset: the SELECT trial (n=17,604) [2] confirmed a 20% reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events over 39.8 months.

Semaglutide mimics the incretin hormone GLP-1, binding to GLP-1 receptors at three sites that each do something different. In the pancreas, receptor activation triggers glucose-dependent insulin secretion. Blood sugar drops, but only when it needs to. That glucose-dependent mechanism is why hypoglycemia is rare as monotherapy. In the gut, semaglutide slows gastric emptying. Food stays in the stomach longer; satiety lasts hours past a meal. This same mechanism causes the nausea during titration. The third site is the hypothalamus. GLP-1 receptor activation in the brain's satiety centers reduces appetite at a neurological level. Community members describe this as "food noise going silent." Obsessive food thoughts quiet within 2 to 4 weeks for most users. A fatty acid side chain (C18 diacid) lets semaglutide bind to serum albumin. That albumin binding slows clearance and extends the half-life to approximately 168 hours (7 days). Subcutaneous bioavailability sits at 89% (FDA prescribing information, Section 12.3). Peak plasma concentration arrives 1 to 3 days post-injection. In SELECT [2], the cardiovascular benefit held across baseline weight and waist size (prespecified SELECT adiposity analysis, Lancet 2025) [9]. That points to effects beyond weight loss alone, but the label says the exact mechanism of the CV benefit has not been established.
Semaglutide benefits center on sustained weight loss, cardiovascular protection, and glycemic control across three FDA-approved indications.
14.9% mean weight loss at 68 weeks (STEP 1, n=1,961) [1]. About 3 in 10 patients on 2.4 mg lost 20% or more (30.2% on the FDA label).
Heart protection too. SELECT confirmed 20% fewer heart attacks, strokes, and cardiovascular deaths in 17,604 people over a mean of 39.8 months [2].
A1c drops 1.4 to 1.9 points on Ozempic 1 mg across the SUSTAIN trials on the FDA label, with weight loss on top.
The 7.2 mg high-dose version pushed weight loss to 18.7% at 72 weeks in STEP UP (n=1,407) [6], vs 15.6% on 2.4 mg. On the label, 45.5% of patients on 7.2 mg lost 20% or more.

Reduced alcohol cravings are widely and consistently reported across community forums. A small 2025 trial in 48 adults with alcohol use disorder [4] found low-dose semaglutide cut drinks per drinking day and craving.
In OASIS 4 (n=307) [7], an oral 25 mg tablet (Wegovy pill, approved December 2025) produced 13.6% weight loss at 64 weeks. Placebo patients lost 2.2%. Its self-pay starting price is $149 per month.
Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 16 key studies · FDA-approved
Unambiguous efficacy across three FDA indications (obesity, T2D, CV risk reduction).

Dosing studied: 0.25 mg → 2.4 mg weekly SC (Wegovy obesity label); 0.25 mg → 2.0 mg weekly SC (Ozempic T2D label); 0.25 mg → 7.2 mg weekly SC (Wegovy HD, March 2026); 1.5 mg → 25 mg daily oral (Wegovy tablets, Dec 2025).

Most well-studied weight-loss drug in modern medicine with 15%+ mean weight loss in RCTs, 20% MACE reduction in SELECT (n=17,604), and a new 7.2 mg dose achieving 18.7% loss in STEP UP (FDA-approved March 2026). Evidence base is the strongest of any weight-loss intervention.
Key Study

STEP 1 (NEJM 2021, PMID 33567185): n=1,961, 14.9% mean weight loss at 68 wk vs. 2.4% placebo. SELECT (NEJM 2023, PMID 37952131): n=17,604, HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.72–0.90) for MACE. STEP UP (Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2025, PMID 40961952): n=1,407, 18.7% loss with 7.2 mg at 72 wk vs. 15.6% with 2.4 mg. OASIS 4 (NEJM 2025, PMID 40934115): oral 25 mg, 13.6% weight loss at 64 wk.
Limitations

Two-thirds of weight regained within 1 year of stopping (STEP 1 extension, PMID 35441470). ~25–40% of weight lost is lean mass without active resistance training. Black box warning for thyroid C-cell tumors (rodent data; human risk unknown). Long-term data beyond 4 years limited. Dysesthesia in 22% at 7.2 mg vs. 6% at 2.4 mg and 0.3% on placebo (FDA label).
Community Experience
Highest-discussed weight-loss intervention on Reddit by a wide margin (350k+ combined members across r/Ozempic and r/semaglutide).

Community dosing: 250–2400 mcg/week for compounded vial users; brand pen users follow FDA titration (0.25–2.4 mg). A growing minority reports sub-therapeutic "microdoses" of 100–250 mcg/week for maintenance appetite control post-weight-loss: no clinical data supports this use case.

Broadly positive: appetite suppression ("food noise going silent") is the defining experience. Primary concerns: GI side effects during titration, cost, lean mass loss, and dread of weight regain after stopping.

Science & Community Aligned

Science and community strongly agree on efficacy magnitude, GI side effect profile, and weight regain kinetics after stopping. Primary divergence: the community endorses microdosing and dose-splitting with no clinical support. Community appetite-suppression reports sometimes exceed trial averages: consistent with satisfaction-bias in self-reporting. Community is ahead of clinical guidelines on lean mass loss awareness; the resistance training + protein co-intervention recommendation spread through Reddit before it entered mainstream prescribing guidance.

Semaglutide ships in pre-filled brand pens (Wegovy, Ozempic, Wegovy HD) that require no reconstitution. For compounded vials, the math matters. 5 mg vial reconstituted with 2 mL bacteriostatic water = 2,500 mcg/mL. On a 100-unit insulin syringe, each unit equals 25 mcg. So your 250 mcg starting dose is 10 units; 500 mcg is 20 units; 1,000 mcg is 40 units; 2,400 mcg maintenance is 96 units. 10 mg vial in 2 mL = 5,000 mcg/mL. Each unit equals 50 mcg. Starting dose of 250 mcg is 5 units; 500 mcg is 10 units; 1,000 mcg is 20 units; 2,400 mcg is 48 units. Titrate slowly. Four weeks at each dose level is the FDA minimum, but experienced users commonly hold 6 to 8 weeks per step. Rushing the titration is the single most common beginner mistake; it makes nausea worse and does not speed up weight loss. You can always stay at a lower dose if appetite suppression is sufficient. Refrigerate compounded vials at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and use within 6 weeks of reconstitution.
Cycling Protocol
Semaglutide is typically used long-term. Weight regain commonly occurs after discontinuation. Discuss with your provider before stopping.
Semaglutide Continuous

Semaglutide is designed for indefinite long-term use: there is no pharmacological rationale for cycling on/off (no receptor desensitization, hormonal axis suppression, or antibody formation that would improve with breaks). Its listed cycle (52 weeks on, no scheduled off period) reflects a continuous-use medication. Cycling framing here applies only to scheduled safety monitoring intervals (labs every 3–6 months, body composition every 6 months) and formal dose re-evaluation periods. Weight regain is rapid on discontinuation: the concept of "cycling off" is medically counterproductive for most patients.
Weight regain beginning within 4–6 weeks of dose reduction or discontinuation

Label titration: 1.5 mg → 4 mg → 9 mg → 25 mg daily, 30 days per step. Oral bioavailability is about 1–2% (SNAC-mediated) vs. 89% for SC injection. In adults without type 2 diabetes, 25 mg daily gives blood levels similar to 2.4 mg weekly SC. The label allows switching between the two.

Must be taken fasted with ≤4 oz plain water, ≥30 min before any food, other liquids, or oral medications. SNAC absorption enhancer is sensitive to food, coffee, juice, and other pills. Works With
Resistance Training + High-Protein Diet (1.2–1.6 g/kg/day)

GLP-1 agonists cause ~25–40% lean mass loss alongside fat. Resistance training 2–3×/week and high protein intake are the primary countermeasures. Clinical guidelines increasingly call this standard of care with any GLP-1 prescription.
Metformin
Standard T2D combination. Complementary mechanisms (hepatic glucose output vs. incretin pathway). No overlapping toxicity. Most T2D patients continue both indefinitely.
SGLT2 Inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, canagliflozin)
Independent CV and renal benefits additive to semaglutide. SGLT2i add renal protection and modest weight loss. Common combination post-SELECT for cardiometabolic patients.
Psyllium Husk / Fiber Supplement
Proactive management of constipation: the most prevalent GI side effect. Community consensus: start fiber at treatment initiation before constipation develops, not reactively.
Avoid
Other GLP-1 receptor agonists (liraglutide, dulaglutide, exenatide)
Overlapping mechanism doubles GI side effects without proportional benefit. Switch sequentially: do not use concurrently.
Tirzepatide (concurrent use)
GLP-1 receptor overlap: combining adds GI toxicity without additive benefit. Tirzepatide is a valid switch option if response to semaglutide is inadequate, but the two drugs must not overlap.
Insulin (without dose adjustment)
Semaglutide enhances endogenous insulin secretion. Adding to existing insulin without reducing the insulin dose risks hypoglycemia. Standard: reduce insulin 20–30% at semaglutide initiation.
Warfarin
Delayed gastric emptying alters absorption timing and may destabilize INR. Monitor INR more frequently during semaglutide initiation and each dose increase.

Generic / Research

No FDA-approved generic semaglutide. Apotex holds a tentative approval for generic semaglutide injection (ANDA 220314, April 2026), which cannot launch while patents or exclusivity block it. Black box warning: semaglutide causes thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents. Whether it causes medullary thyroid carcinoma in humans is unknown. Anyone with a personal or family history of MTC or MEN2 cannot use this drug. That warning is printed on every Wegovy and Ozempic label, and it stays there. GI side effects dominate the titration period. Nausea hits 40 to 50% of patients during the first weeks at each new dose level. For some, that nausea is severe enough to impact daily function and work productivity. Community consensus recommends extending each titration step to 6 to 8 weeks rather than 4 if nausea is bad. The nausea typically fades within the first week at each stable dose. Constipation hit 24% of adults on Wegovy 2.4 mg in the label's weight trials (11% on placebo). Community reports describe it as common with long-term use. Proactive fiber supplementation (psyllium husk from day one) is the top community recommendation. Magnesium citrate at 200 to 400 mg before bed serves as the standard backup. Vomiting and diarrhea also occur, usually transiently during dose escalation. Rare but serious: pancreatitis requires immediate emergency evaluation if you experience severe abdominal pain radiating to the back. Gallbladder disease (cholelithiasis, cholecystitis) is a known complication, particularly with rapid weight loss. Acute kidney injury can result from dehydration driven by persistent GI symptoms. The US labels flag three more signals. Ileus (intestinal obstruction) appears in postmarketing reports and requires emergency care if you develop severe persistent abdominal pain. Diabetic retinopathy complications can paradoxically worsen with rapid A1c improvement in patients with pre-existing retinopathy. Resting heart rate increases a mean 1 to 4 bpm. In the Wegovy weight trials, 26% of users (vs 16% on placebo) had a rise of 20 bpm or more at some visit. NAION (non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy) is a separate, rarer eye signal. It's a loss of blood flow to the front of the optic nerve that can cause sudden, painless vision loss, usually in one eye. A 2026 meta-analysis pooled 8 observational cohort studies covering 5,916,559 people [5]. Semaglutide users had roughly double the risk (relative effect 1.93, 95% CI 1.22 to 3.08). The studies disagreed widely (I² 91%), and the link was significant in people with diabetes but not in the overweight or obesity subgroup. These are associations, not proof that semaglutide causes NAION. The current US Wegovy, Ozempic, and Rybelsus labels don't list it. Europe's EMA called it a very rare side effect in June 2025 (up to 1 in 10,000 people). Sudden vision loss or fast-worsening eyesight on semaglutide needs same-day medical care. The 7.2 mg Wegovy HD dose introduced a new signal, dysesthesia (altered skin sensation such as tingling or burning). In the label's trials it hit 22% of patients on 7.2 mg, vs 6% on 2.4 mg and 0.3% on placebo. Among those affected, 18% had not recovered by the end of the trial. Hair thinning from telogen effluvium peaks between months 3 and 6. It is a response to rapid weight loss, not a direct drug effect. It typically resolves by month 8 to 12 with adequate protein intake. Lean mass loss of 25 to 40% of total weight lost is documented without resistance training. "Ozempic face" (facial volume loss) becomes visible after 30+ lbs of weight loss. The label contraindications are a personal or family history of MTC or MEN2 and serious hypersensitivity to semaglutide. For weight loss, the label says to stop it in pregnancy, and at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy. It advises against breastfeeding on the tablets and doesn't recommend semaglutide with severe gastroparesis. A history of pancreatitis warrants a talk with your prescriber first. If you are on insulin or sulfonylureas, doses of those drugs typically need a 20 to 30% reduction at semaglutide initiation to prevent hypoglycemia.
Common Issues & Solutions

Persistent nausea: Do not escalate the dose. Hold the current level for an additional 4 weeks. Eat small, bland, low-fat meals. Ginger (chews, tea) has antiemetic evidence. Discuss ondansetron (Zofran) with prescriber for the first 48–72 hours at each new dose level. If nausea is severe, step back one dose level and re-titrate more slowly: a 6–8 week hold per step instead of 4 weeks is widely used by the community.

Constipation (24% in the label's trials; common in community reports): Start psyllium husk fiber (1 tbsp in water daily) from day one: before constipation develops. Hydrate actively; semaglutide can suppress thirst signals. Magnesium citrate (200–400 mg at bedtime) is the standard community backup. Polyethylene glycol (MiraLAX) is safe for regular use. If none of these work within 1 week, contact prescriber.

Weight loss plateau: Expected as body adapts to a new set point. If stalled at current dose for 4+ weeks, continue titrating per schedule. If stalled at 2.4 mg for ≥3 months, discuss with provider: Wegovy HD (7.2 mg) is now FDA-approved. Re-audit caloric intake: TDEE decreases as body weight falls and portions may need to shrink further even if appetite remains suppressed.

Lean mass loss ("skinny fat" outcome): Add resistance training 2–3×/week and target protein intake of 1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight daily. Get a DEXA scan at baseline for reference. This co-intervention is now in clinical prescribing guidelines: not optional if long-term body composition matters.

Hair thinning (months 3–6): Telogen effluvium from rapid weight loss, not a direct pharmacological effect of semaglutide. Temporary: typically resolves by months 8–12. Ensure adequate protein (≥80 g/day) and consider biotin supplementation. If hair loss continues beyond 12 months, test thyroid function and serum ferritin.

Semaglutide is FDA-approved in four products. Ozempic (type 2 diabetes) came in December 2017 and Rybelsus (oral, type 2 diabetes) in September 2019. Wegovy injection (chronic weight management) followed in June 2021, and Wegovy tablets on December 22, 2025. Wegovy later added cardiovascular risk reduction (March 2024, from SELECT) and MASH with liver fibrosis (August 2025, accelerated approval). The 7.2 mg Wegovy HD dose followed in March 2026. Ozempic added a kidney disease indication in January 2025 (FLOW), and Rybelsus added cardiovascular risk reduction in October 2025. Compounded semaglutide entered a complex legal environment. The FDA removed semaglutide from its drug shortage list on February 21, 2025. Enforcement deadlines followed: 503A compounding pharmacies faced an April 22, 2025 cutoff, 503B outsourcing facilities faced May 22, 2025. Compounded GLP-1 marketing continued after those dates. FDA sent warning letters to companies marketing compounded GLP-1 drugs on September 9, 2025, and warned 30 more telehealth companies on March 3, 2026. Novo Nordisk sued a large telehealth compounder for patent infringement in February 2026. Legal status remains in flux. Semaglutide is not on WADA's 2026 Prohibited List. WADA's 2026 Monitoring Program tracks markers of semaglutide and tirzepatide in and out of competition. Monitoring watches for misuse without banning the drug. No FDA-approved generic exists. Apotex holds a tentative approval for generic semaglutide injection (ANDA 220314, April 2026), which cannot launch while patents or exclusivity block it. protocols.goal: Weight Loss: Standard (Wegovy 2.4 mg FDA Label)

phases.name: Titration Step 1
phases.syringeUnits: 10 units (5 mg/2 mL vial); 5 units (10 mg/2 mL vial)
phases.timing: Same day each week; abdomen, thigh, or upper arm; rotate sites
phases.notes: Sub-therapeutic tolerability dose. No weight loss expected: primes GI receptors for higher doses. Do not skip this step.

phases.name: Titration Step 2
phases.syringeUnits: 20 units (5 mg/2 mL vial); 10 units (10 mg/2 mL vial)
phases.notes: First pharmacologically active dose. Appetite suppression becomes noticeable. Early weight loss of 2–4% from baseline.

phases.name: Titration Step 3
phases.syringeUnits: 40 units (5 mg/2 mL vial); 20 units (10 mg/2 mL vial)
phases.notes: Ozempic T2D therapeutic range. Steady weight loss; most patients at 5–8% loss from baseline by end of this phase.

phases.name: Titration Step 4
phases.syringeUnits: 68 units (5 mg/2 mL vial); 34 units (10 mg/2 mL vial)
phases.notes: Penultimate step. Strong hunger reduction. Most patients tolerate this well if prior steps were not rushed.

phases.name: Maintenance
phases.syringeUnits: 96 units (5 mg/2 mL vial); 48 units (10 mg/2 mL vial)
phases.notes: Full therapeutic dose. STEP 1: 14.9% mean weight loss at 68 weeks. 30.2% of patients lost ≥20% (FDA label). Weight loss rate decelerates after week 40.

protocols.monitoringNotes: HbA1c, lipid panel, CMP (renal function) at baseline and every 3–6 months. Resting heart rate at every visit. DEXA body composition at baseline and every 6 months.

protocols.goal: Weight Loss: High Dose (Wegovy HD 7.2 mg, FDA-approved March 2026)

phases.name: Standard Titration (Steps 1–5)
phases.dose: 0.25 mg → 0.5 mg → 1.0 mg → 1.7 mg → 2.4 mg (4 weeks each step)
phases.notes: Full standard Wegovy titration is required, with at least 4 weeks at 2.4 mg, before moving to 7.2 mg. Cannot be skipped.

phases.name: HD Maintenance
phases.notes: Maximum approved dose. The label moves straight from 2.4 mg to 7.2 mg, with no intermediate step. That move needs at least 4 weeks on 2.4 mg and a clinical need for more weight loss. STEP UP: 18.7% mean weight loss at 72 wk. Dysesthesia signal: 22% at this dose vs. 6% at 2.4 mg and 0.3% on placebo (FDA label): monitor and document. Supplied as the single-dose Wegovy HD pen.

protocols.monitoringNotes: Same as standard Wegovy protocol plus: mandatory DEXA body composition every 6 months given higher lean mass loss risk. Neurological assessment if dysesthesia symptoms (tingling, numbness) develop.

phases.name: Titration
phases.notes: Tolerability only, not therapeutic for blood sugar control.

phases.name: First Therapeutic Dose
phases.notes: Evaluate A1c after 8–12 weeks. Many T2D patients reach target A1c at this dose and stay here.

phases.name: Escalation (if needed)
phases.dose: 1.0 mg → 2.0 mg (if A1c target not met)
phases.syringeUnits: 40 units at 1.0 mg; 80 units at 2.0 mg (5 mg/2 mL vial)
phases.notes: SUSTAIN trials on the Ozempic label: 1.0 mg reduces A1c by 1.4–1.9%. 2.0 mg added in 2022 Ozempic label update for additional glycemic control. Also reduces risk of CKD progression (FLOW trial, Jan 2025 new indication).

protocols.monitoringNotes: A1c every 3 months until stable, then every 6 months. Monitor eGFR: AKI risk from GI-driven dehydration. If on insulin or sulfonylureas, reduce those doses at initiation to prevent hypoglycemia.

protocols.goal: Cardiovascular Risk Reduction (SELECT: non-diabetic adults with obesity or overweight + established CVD)

phases.name: Titration
phases.dose: 0.25 mg → 0.5 mg → 1.0 mg → 1.7 mg (4 weeks each)
phases.notes: Standard Wegovy titration required. No shortcuts to the maintenance dose.

phases.name: CV Maintenance
phases.syringeUnits: 96 units (5 mg/2 mL vial); 48 units (10 mg/2 mL vial)
phases.notes: SELECT ran a mean of 39.8 months at 2.4 mg. The MACE benefit (HR 0.80) held across baseline weight and waist size (prespecified SELECT adiposity analysis, Lancet 2025, PMID 41138739). It did not track weight loss. The label says the exact mechanism of the CV benefit has not been established. FDA CV indication granted March 8, 2024.

protocols.duration: 16 weeks titration + indefinite maintenance (SELECT mean 39.8 months)
protocols.monitoringNotes: Standard CV monitoring: lipids, blood pressure, hs-CRP. SELECT showed improvements in waist circumference, systolic BP, CRP, and triglycerides across the maintenance period. Heart rate monitoring is critical: flag any sustained increase >15 bpm from baseline.

faqs.q: What is the recommended semaglutide dosage for weight loss?
faqs.a: The Wegovy label starts at 0.25 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then titrates through 0.5 mg, 1.0 mg, and 1.7 mg before reaching the maintenance dose of 2.4 mg weekly. After at least 4 weeks on 2.4 mg, the label allows 7.2 mg weekly if more weight loss is needed. STEP UP saw 18.7% weight loss with it. Each dose step lasts 4 weeks minimum.

faqs.q: What are the side effects of semaglutide?
faqs.a: Nausea affects about 44% of users on Wegovy 2.4 mg, vs 16% on placebo (FDA label). Vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation are also common in the first 8 weeks. Rare but serious risks include acute pancreatitis (0.2 cases per 100 patient-years) and gallstones (1.6% vs 0.7% on placebo). There's also the FDA black box warning for medullary thyroid carcinoma risk, based on rodent models. GI symptoms usually fade after the body adjusts to each dose level.

Semaglutide mimics the GLP-1 hormone. It binds GLP-1 receptors in the pancreas to stimulate insulin release and in the brain to reduce appetite. The half-life is about 7 days, which allows once-weekly dosing. A C18 fatty acid chain lets it bind albumin, which slows clearance, and a change at position 8 protects it from DPP-4 (FDA label).

Yes. Semaglutide is FDA-approved in four products. They are Ozempic (type 2 diabetes, 2017), Rybelsus (oral tablet for diabetes, 2019), Wegovy injection (weight management, 2021), and Wegovy tablets (December 2025). The 7.2 mg Wegovy HD dose followed in March 2026. The SELECT trial also established cardiovascular risk reduction in 17,604 patients.

faqs.q: What happens when you stop semaglutide?
faqs.a: The STEP 1 extension trial showed that roughly two-thirds of lost weight returned within one year of stopping (PMID 35441470). Appetite signals normalize as GLP-1 receptor stimulation ends. The usual options are long-term maintenance dosing or a planned taper with diet and exercise support.

Semaglutide earns an A on the Peptide Schedule safety scale, backed by four FDA approvals and the 17,604-patient SELECT outcomes trial, though a black box warning for rodent thyroid C-cell tumors stays on every label. The most common problem is gastrointestinal, with nausea affecting about 44% of users during titration and constipation affecting roughly a quarter of users long-term. Pancreatitis and gallbladder disease are rare but serious, and a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 rules it out.
Semaglutide typically comes in 5mg or 10mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Semaglutide?
faqs.a: The half-life of Semaglutide is ~7 days. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist with four FDA approvals and the largest cardiovascular outcomes trial ever run for a weight loss drug. The STEP 1 trial showed 14.9% mean weight loss at 68 weeks in 1,961 adults, and the newer 7.2 mg dose pushed that to 18.7% in STEP UP. The SELECT trial (17,604 participants) showed a 20% reduction in heart attacks, strokes, and cardiovascular death. Brand pricing runs $1,349 per month, though the oral tablet approved in December 2025 brought self-pay costs down to $149 per month. GI side effects are common during dose titration, and roughly two-thirds of the weight returns within a year of stopping.
